slides.title:
The drink isn't
the afterthought here.
slides.body:
In most Korean drinking houses the food is anju — something to eat so the drinking can continue. The MICHELIN Guide describes this room the other way round: banju culture read through a contemporary lens, with a wide makgeolli selection and dishes designed to complement it.

The signatures the guide lists — house-made tofu with saeujeot kimchi, pork belly, pollock roe — are built around contrast in texture rather than heat.

caption:
In most Korean bars the food is anju — something to eat so the drinking can continue. One Itaewon room reads it the other way.

Mr. Ahn's Craft Makgeolli, on Gyeongnidan-gil, pairs artisan makgeolli with dishes built to complement it. The MICHELIN Guide lists it Bib Gourmand. About five tables, so book ahead.

Hours and menus change — worth confirming first.
